title: Soft agar colony formation assay to quantify mouse embryonic fibroblast transformation after Salmonella infection
protocol: Subculture bacteria until an optical density (OD600) of 2 is reached, optimal for cell infection.
Dilute 150 μL of overnight bacterial culture in 5 mL of LB medium in a centrifuge tube supplemented with the appropriate antibiotic if necessary.
Incubate diluted bacterial culture at 37°C on an orbital shaker set to 220 rpm for 3 hours.
Warm up growth media (DMEM-, DMEM+FBS+Gent100, and DMEM+FBS+Gent10) to a stable temperature of 37°C.
Melt 3% soft agar solution using a microwave.
Swirl the melting 3% soft agar solution every 10-20 seconds to avoid clumps.
Cool down a 3% soft agar solution using a 42°C water bath or ThermoMixer at 300 rpm.
Dilute 5 mL of the 3% soft agar solution in 16.5 mL of DMEM+FBS+Gent to prepare the 0.7% agar bottom layer.
Mix the diluted solution gently by pipetting up and down until homogeneous, avoiding bubbles.
Pour 3 mL of the mixture into each well of a 6-well plate, ensuring the bottom is completely covered without air bubbles.
Fill the pipette with 1 extra mL to avoid emptying it completely when filling the well.
Transfer the 6-well plate to a flat shelf in a fridge at 4°C and let cool for 20 minutes until fully solidified.
Place the 6-well plate into an incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2, with internal humidity of approximately 90%.
Measure the concentration of bacteria at the end of the 3 h bacterial subculture.
Fill a cuvette with 1 mL LB medium.
Blank the spectrophotometer.
Mix 200 μL of the bacterial subculture with 800 μL of LB medium in a cuvette.
Seal the cuvette with parafilm and measure the OD600.
Transfer 1 mL of the bacterial subculture to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Spin down for 1 min at 9000 g.
Aspirate the supernatant (LB medium).
Wash the bacteria with 1 mL of pre-warmed DMEM-.
Spin down for 1 min at 9000 g.
Aspirate the supernatant (DMEM-).
Resuspend the bacterial pellet in 1 mL of pre-warmed DMEM-.
Calculate the required volume of bacterial subculture based on OD600 and conversion factor.
Dilute 7 μL of washed bacterial subculture into 1.143 mL of DMEM- to create infection mix.
Add 0.5 ml of infection mix to cells designated for infected conditions.
Remove cell medium from wells in a 12-well plate.
Add 0.5 ml of pre-warmed DMEM- to cells designated for non-infected conditions.
Place the plate back into the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 30 minutes.
Wash infected cells twice with pre-warmed DMEM-.
Add 1 mL of pre-warmed DMEM+FBS+Gent100 per well to all wells.
Incubate the plate in the incubator at 37°C, 5% CO2 for 1 hour.
Aspirate the medium from each well.
Wash each well with 1 mL of PBS.
Remove PBS.
Add 200 μL of trypsin per well.
Incubate the cells for 5 min at 37°C.
Verify that cells are ready to detach using a bench microscope.
Add 800 μL of DMEM+FBS per well to stop trypsin action.
Resuspend cells and transfer 2 wells corresponding to one condition into a 15 mL centrifuge tube (total 2 mL per tube).
Spin down the tubes at 300 g for 4 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend each pellet in 1 mL of DMEM+FBS+Gent10.
Count cells for each condition using an appropriate method.
Transfer 2 × 10^5 cells from each condition into a new 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Complete the volume to 6.8 mL with DMEM+FBS+Gent10 for each condition.
Add 1.2 mL of melted 3% soft agar to one cell-containing centrifuge tube to achieve a final agar concentration of 0.45% and a total volume of 8 mL.
Using a 5 mL pipette, take 2.5 mL of the cell and agar-containing solution.
Pass the cells through a 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom tube with cell-strainer cap.
Collect the solution in the round-bottom tube and pass it through a second cell strainer cap.
Use the pipetboy gently to avoid bubbles.
Pour 2 mL of the solution on top of the agar bottom layer.
Repeat steps 29–32 twice more starting from the same cell and agar-containing tube to fill 3 wells of the 6-well plate per condition.
Carefully transfer the 6-well plate to a flat shelf of a fridge at 4°C.
Let the plate cool down for 20 minutes until the top layer is fully solidified.
Fill the spaces between the wells with sterile water or PBS to prevent fast drying of the agar gel.
Incubate at 37°C for 2–3 weeks (or until cell colonies are visible).
Acquire the 6-well plate using the GelCount device and GelCount Software when small cell colonies are visible.
Turn on the GelCount device using the back on/off button.
Check the plate regularly with a cell culture microscope to see if cell colonies start forming.
Extract the 6-well plate tray and place it under the hood.
Wipe the bottom of the 6-well plate(s) with 70% ethanol to remove dust.
Place the 6-well plate(s) within the tray and take a picture of the plate positions.
Take off the cap of the 6-well plate(s).
Insert the tray with the plate within the GelCount device and press the central button to close the device.
On the GelCount software, select the number of plates to acquire.
Press “acquire only”.
Save the files.
Perform quantitative analysis of cell colonies at a later time on an off-line computer equipped with GelCount software.
